subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as gateway-attested connect metadata, an explicitly untrusted client hint, or not exposed to agents yet?
rationale: Agents could use this field for native-only UX, deep links, diagnostics, or capability decisions, so automation should not choose the trust semantics or carrier shape without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Gateway-attested metadata
options.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust.

options.title: Untrusted diagnostic hint
options.body: Expose a clearly labeled untrusted client hint only for debugging and forbid capability or permission decisions from it.

options.title: Decline runtime exposure
options.body: Keep client identity limited to Gateway connection diagnostics until a stronger client-attestation design exists.

recommendation.title: Gateway-attested metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may trust.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history points to the Gateway protocol/client metadata boundary that would own this decision.
